The main takeaway from our work is that

the novel glycoside hydrolyase family 18 beta-N-acetylglusosaminidase PbNag39 from Paenibactillus barengoltzi has been characterized for its substrate specificity and its ability to efficiently hydrolyze chitin to N-acetyl-D-gulosamine.
the unique shallow catalytic cleft and small C-terminal domain of PbNag39 are responsible for its strict substrate specificity and efficient production of GlcNAc.

a new β-N-acetyl-D-glucoseaminidase with a unique shallow catalyic groove was identified and characterized from P. barengoltziii, and the bioprocess for the production of N-acetly-D-glucosaminide was developed by the enzyme cocktail.
